<div class="review-text">
Flowers for Algernon was an absolutely extraordinary read which prodded at science fiction in a way I had never seen before. Sure, Daniel Keyes was a little bit a product of his time and could be frustrating occasionally, but for the most part he was very conscientious, doing a better job of writing about a lot of sensitive and confusing topics than you ever see addressed in even abstract ways today.<br>
The book was very raw and emotionally visceral in a lot of segments, and although it was sort of overbearing at times it made the experience overall very engaging. <a class="review-spoiler-link" href="https://www.goodreads.com/review/show/5790209481">(view spoiler)</a><br>
Overall, this ended up being one of the most gratifying reads I've had the pleasure of considering for a long time, and it filled a niche I feel as if I had been searching for over the course of many years. This was such a unique experience that I would easily recommend Flowers for Algernon under the majority of circumstances.
</div>
